Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s **Code** tab, open `_config.yml` and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserve unrelated settings; do not add a second `chulapa-skin` section.

## Enable palette generation

Set `autothemer` to the YAML boolean `true` and supply a quoted main color. For a palette without a predefined skin’s color assignments, use `none`:

```
chulapa-skin:
  skin: none
  autothemer: true
  vars:
    primary: "#285d70"

```

`none` changes the selected skin; use it only if that is your intention. To keep your current skin, preserve its name instead. Autothemer can work with a skin, but it only fills undefined values. Existing skin colors and `vars` overrides remain in effect. Keep other custom variables unless you mean to remove them.

To stop this extra palette-generation step, omit `autothemer` or set it to `false` without quotes. A `skin: auto` selection separately loads the generator; [the reference](./03-theming#autothemer) distinguishes the two settings.

## Publish and check

Check the main color, backgrounds, warnings, errors and text contrast across your pages. If a color does not change, check whether your skin or `vars` already sets it. This page lists appearance settings. For a task, use [Choose a skin](./22-choose-skin), [Change a color](./23-change-color), [Change fonts](./24-change-fonts) or [Change code highlighting](./25-code-highlighting). For relationships between settings, read [How skins and overrides interact](./26-appearance-precedence). For custom Sass and the Codeply sandbox, use [Adapt a Sass skin](./28-custom-skin).

Settings belong in `_config.yml` and compile into CSS during the build. Local preview needs a Jekyll restart after configuration changes.

## Skins

| Field             | Values / default                                                                         | Constraint                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| chulapa-skin.skin | Exact skin filename without .scss; default none. Examples: journal, gitdev, lux, flatly. | Names are case-sensitive on case-sensitive filesystems; unknown names fail the Sass import. |
| skin: none        | No predefined skin assignments.                                                          | Bootstrap/theme defaults and explicit vars still apply.                                     |
| skin: auto        | Loads the generated palette as the selected skin.

## Code highlighting

`chulapa-skin.highlight` selects a highlighting stylesheet; its default is `default`. The setting selects appearance, while Rouge performs syntax highlighting. [Style specimens](./syntax-highlighting) show the available styles. Procedure: [Change code highlighting](./25-code-highlighting).

## Autothemer

`chulapa-skin.autothemer` enables the palette-generation step after skin and `vars` when set to the YAML boolean `true`; omit it or use `false` to disable that step. It is independent of `skin: auto`. Its default primary color is Bootstrap 4’s `#007bff` when not already assigned.

Existing skin and `vars` assignments remain in effect. Procedure: [Enable Autothemer](./27-autothemer). Rationale: [How skins and overrides interact](./26-appearance-precedence).

## Variables

`chulapa-skin.vars` is a mapping of supported Bootstrap/theme Sass variable names to Sass expressions. Names omit the leading `$` and trailing `;`. Hex colors, font lists and sizes are quoted strings; switches such as `enable-rounded` are YAML booleans. For example:

```

  vars:
    body-bg: "#000"
    body-color: "#eee"
    font-family-base: "Montserrat"

```

The corresponding Sass assignments are `$body-bg: #000;`, `$body-color: #eee;`and `$font-family-base: Montserrat;`. A font stylesheet is a separate input; [the fonts guide](./24-change-fonts) includes a complete loading/application example.

The [variable dictionary](./variable-dictionary) lists common inputs; [Bootstrap’s variable source](https://github.com/dieghernan/chulapa/blob/main/%5Fsass/bootstrap/%5Fvariables.scss)contains the full Bootstrap definitions. A skin provides a coordinated starting design. Individual variables customize that design; Autothemer supplies a generated palette for values that are still undefined. These choices affect appearance rather than the content layout.

## Why a color change can leave other colors unchanged

The selected skin supplies variable assignments first. Values in `chulapa-skin.vars` override those assignments. Autothemer follows, using defaults that preserve values already assigned by either source. Bootstrap and the theme’s components then use those values to produce the stylesheet.

That is why changing `primary` does not promise a complete recoloring of an existing skin. If it explicitly assigns a warning color or navbar background, that component can retain its own color. Autothemer fills gaps; it does not replace an existing palette. A skin written with `!default` allows subsequent configuration overrides while cooperating with the default palette.

Without an explicit skin/variable value, the navbar background uses `primary`; the footer and hero inherit the navbar background, and the landing page inherits the hero background. Many text colors are derived from backgrounds. Explicit component values take precedence over these defaults.

Hex colors and Sass expressions such as sizes/font lists are quoted strings; switches are YAML booleans. Names omit the Sass `$` prefix and trailing semicolon. For editing and publishing, use [Change a color](./23-change-color)or [Change fonts](./24-change-fonts). Mapping syntax specimen:

```
chulapa-skin:
  vars:
    primary: "#345678"

```

Precedence and inherited values: [How skins and overrides interact](./26-appearance-precedence).

## Chulapa\-specific variables

## Let visitors switch between light and dark

Available in **2.2.0** and later. The v2.1.0 gem and pinned remote theme do not include this feature.

In `_config.yml`, keep your existing `chulapa-skin` section for the light appearance. Add a separate `chulapa-skin-dark` section for the dark appearance. For example, this complete pair uses matching GitDev skins:

```
chulapa-skin:
  skin: gitdev
  highlight: github
chulapa-skin-dark:
  skin: gitdev-dark
  highlight: github.dark

```

Both sections support `skin`, `highlight`, `vars` and `autothemer` with the [same precedence rules](./26-appearance-precedence). Each section is independent: copy shared font or color overrides into both if needed. The dark highlighter uses `chulapa-skin.highlight` when `chulapa-skin-dark.highlight` is omitted, then `default` if neither is set. Other settings are independent. An unknown skin or highlighter name fails the build.

After publishing, the navigation shows an icon for the current mode, with **Light**, **Dark** and **Auto** choices in a dropdown. This works with classic, floating and dual navigation, including sites without menu links. If you set `vars.primary` in either skin, its value also supplies the browser’s address-bar color when that appearance is active, on browsers that support it. A skin without an explicit `vars.primary` leaves that color to the browser. The selector preserves custom `theme-color` tags added through the head hook. The footer credits both configured built-in skins, once each.

Light is the initial default. Auto follows the device’s color preference and updates when it changes. The browser remembers the visitor’s choice across pages and tabs. If browser storage is blocked, switching still works on the current page but the preference cannot be remembered.

```yml
chulapa-skin:
  skin: none
  autothemer: true
  vars:
    primary: "#7A288A"
```

Choose families at [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/) and use their stylesheet URL. Add the URL to the existing `googlefonts` list, then set the families under your existing `chulapa-skin.vars`. For example:

```
googlefonts:
  - url: "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Raleway&family=Rubik&display=swap"

chulapa-skin:
  skin: journal

    font-family-base: "Rubik, sans-serif"
    headings-font-family: "Raleway, sans-serif"

```

Each skin already has a font choice; changing fonts is optional. For the bundled font rather than an external stylesheet, use [the bundled-font guide](./53-chulapa-font).

No additional font configuration is needed for those defaults.

## Load and apply the fonts

Choose families at [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/) and use their stylesheet URL. Add the URL to the existing `googlefonts` list, then set the families under your existing `chulapa-skin.vars`. For example:

```
googlefonts:
  - url: "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Raleway&family=Rubik&display=swap"

chulapa-skin:
  skin: journal
  vars:
    font-family-base: "Rubik, sans-serif"
    headings-font-family: "Raleway, sans-serif"

```

Keep your selected skin and other variables. The stylesheet loads the families; `font-family-base` applies Rubik to body text and `headings-font-family` applies Raleway to headings. Loading a font alone does not apply it.

## Let visitors switch between light and dark

Available in **2.2.0** and later. The v2.1.0 gem and pinned remote theme do not include this feature.

description: Keep theme templates while connecting an existing website - Use this guide if you already have a website configured with Welcomments, its website ID and a working integration that delivers comment files to this repository. Configure that service-side integration using the provider’s instructions before testing new submissions.
---

 

Use this guide if you already have a website configured with [Welcomments](https://welcomments.io/), its website ID and a working integration that delivers comment files to this repository. Configure that service-side integration using the provider’s instructions before testing new submissions.

## Review the integration files

Review any pull request generated by Welcomments before merging it. Retain the customized `_includes/welcomments/` templates supplied by Chulapa, rather than replacing them with generic provider templates. Review any local copies left by another theme: local files override the installed theme’s files.

Keep the provider’s comment data and repository integration. The theme reads comment data from `_data/welcomments/`; the website ID alone does not deliver that data or configure the external service.

## Select Welcomments

In `_config.yml`, edit the existing `comments` section, or add it once if absent. Replace the example website ID and preserve unrelated settings:

```
comments:
  provider: welcomments
  website_id: "YOUR_WELCOMMENTS_WEBSITE_ID"

```

## Check the form URL on a project site

In v2.2.0, the theme form uses the full published article URL, including `baseurl`. The v2.1.0 form omits that path: for a site such as `https://ana.github.io/my-blog`, its submitted URL can point outside `/my-blog`. description: Check your site’s navigation, colors and resources - Verify your published pages with a keyboard, narrow screens and real content.
---

 

Use this guide to check a published site after changing content, a skin or an integration. Have the home page, a representative article and search open, along with any galleries, videos or comments you use.

Some expected controls require v2.2.0, not the v2.1.0 gem or pin. Compare your installed version with [the behavior reference](./48-accessibility-reference). These checks do not establish WCAG compliance by themselves.

## Check your own pages

Open those pages at a narrow phone width and enlarge their text. Confirm that content remains readable and controls stay reachable. Check long headings and your actual images, not only short sample content. Repeat after fixing a problem.

Use the steps below for each representative page. Record the page, browser, viewport and problem so you can verify the same case after changing it.

## Keyboard navigation

1. Use Tab without a mouse. Confirm you can see which link or control has focus. Activate **Skip to content** when available and check that it bypasses the menu.
2. Open and close your menu and dropdowns. Use Enter for links, Enter/Space for buttons and Escape where a panel supports it. Confirm focus returns to the trigger after closing the floating menu.
3. If you use the sidebar TOC, open it, Tab through its controls and close it with Escape. Check that closed controls are no longer reachable and that section highlighting does not move keyboard focus while you read.
4. In a PhotoSwipe gallery, open an image, browse with arrow keys and close with Escape. Check the return to the image link. Try search, comments and your other widgets too.
